page.layout: One printed page: running head at top, one column of continuous text, a note "alias" in the right margin beside the last line. Left margin shows only faint marks, not text.

main_text.p: rum legatis ad suos relata essent, in proximo conventu eorum, consentientibus omnium civitatum voluntatibus bellum Lacedaemonis indictum: illatumque id statim fuisset, nisi hyems ingruens impedivisset: incursionibus tamen minutis Lacedaemoniorum fines à terrâ & mari vastati. Ad hæc sopienda Romanus consul in Peloponnesum- cum venisset, jussu ejus concilium apud Elidenses indictum, & Lacedaemonii ad disceptandum istuc acciti. Ibi non disceptatione solum, sed etiam altercatione partium, ut inquit Livius, audita aliquandiu, consul satis ambitiosè partem utramque fovendo, incertaque respondendo, demum una denunciatione finem ei imposuit, praecipiens nimirum, ut bello abstinerent, donec Romam legatos ad senatum misissent. Itaque legatio utrimque Romam missa: exulum Laconicorum causa, petentibus ipsis, commendata est Achaeis. Principes legationis Achaeorum fuere Diophanes & Lycortas, Polybii historiae scriptoris pater, uterque Megalopolitanus: quorum ut saepè aliàs, sic hac quoque in re discordes erant sententiae. Diophanes Romam veniens senatui disceptationem rerum omnium permittebat, cum optimè controversias inter Achaeosalias? & La-

page.notes: Running head and page number read from the scan; the "5" of 385 is slightly unclear. The note "alias" in the right margin is faint and may be a reference word. The faint marks down the left margin and the small smudged line at the bottom right ("ɜɛ ɪɪ") look like show-through from the other side of the leaf and are left out. Long s is printed as plain s throughout. "fopienda" and "fæpè" were read with long s and given as sopienda and saepè. The line-end "Peloponnesum-" carries a printed dash, kept as a hyphen. The last line ends mid-word ("La-") and continues on the next page.
